claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page) on the Pulumi docs site, linked from the support index.
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version and which providers get long-term security updates.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The Pulumi provider support policy page (/docs/support/provider-support-policy/) lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry (/registry/) shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (Provider support policy) as a link target.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes made during an update if an error or failure occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`; it compares the desired state to the last recorded state.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes state and applies the desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.
Pulumi auto-naming appends a random suffix to the logical name, and creating the replacement before deleting the old resource enables replacement with less downtime.
Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key per stack for encrypting secrets, configurable to use a custom secrets provider.
`pulumi config set --secret` encrypts the value so it can be persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine; some Pulumi providers use open-source Terraform schemas, while Pulumi native providers map directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in and can be enabled with a flag, command, or environment variable such as `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`.
Experimental features can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle.
The npm tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N-1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
Pulumi's providers receiving long-term support updates on eligible older versions are: AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
The Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/aws/, azure/, azure-native/, azuread/, command/, docker-build/, gcp/, kubernetes/, tls/, and vault/.

The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
Pulumi LTS providers remain compatible with the version of the Pulumi engine they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.

When major N+1 of a covered provider ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the previous LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining time in its 12-month window.
Within the LTS major of a covered provider, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a Pulumi provider (the recommended practice) automatically receive patch releases as they ship.
If v3 is the newest release, v2 is N-1 (LTS), and v1 and earlier are end of life and receive no patches.
The current major (N) of a Pulumi provider receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
The FAQ page at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section 'what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions'.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
